reference_soap.subjective:
Chief Complaint: gritty, burning sensation in both eyes worsening at the end of the day

62F presents with 6 months of bilateral eye burning, dryness, and foreign body sensation that worsens when reading, using the computer, or at the end of the day in dry, air-conditioned rooms.
reference_soap.objective: Complete vital signs and focused physical examination. Evaluate for pertinent signs.
reference_soap.assessment: Clinical presentation highly suggestive of Dry Eye Syndrome (Keratoconjunctivitis Sicca), associated with Sjogren's.
reference_soap.plan: Perform Schirmer testing and ocular-surface staining when indicated. Recommend preservative-free artificial tears, warm compresses, and nighttime lubricating ointment; consider punctal plugs for persistent symptoms. Arrange appropriate retinal screening for ongoing hydroxychloroquine use, and urgently assess pain, photophobia, or reduced vision.

history.answer: My eyes have been burning and feeling gritty for about six months now, and it seems to get worse toward the end of the day.
It started gradually about six months ago and has been constantly bothering me ever since.
It affects both of my eyes equally.
My eyes look a little bloodshot and pink across the whites, but there are no bright red patches or rings around the colored part.
It feels like I have sand or grit stuck in my eyes along with a burning sensation, but I do not have deep aching eye pain.
My vision gets slightly blurry when my eyes feel very dry, but it clears right up when I blink, and my eyesight hasn't worsened overall.
Bright light makes my eyes feel irritated when they are dry, but looking at light does not cause sharp pain.
No, I haven't seen any halos or rainbow rings around lights, and I have no headache, nausea, or vomiting.
I don't have thick yellow pus or crusty discharge, and my eyelids aren't stuck together in the morning. Sometimes I just see a tiny bit of clear, stringy mucus.
No, they don't feel itchy, just gritty and burning.
No, my eyelids are not swollen, and I haven't noticed any lumps, styes, or crusty buildup on my lash line.
Moving my eyes does not hurt at all, my eyes aren't bulging out, and I don't see double.
No, I haven't had a cold, sore throat, or fever recently, and nobody around me has had pink eye.
No, I have never worn contact lenses.
No, I haven't injured my eyes, nothing has splashed into them, and I haven't been around welding sparks or harsh chemicals.
No, it stays about the same all year round, and I don't have seasonal allergies, hay fever, or eczema.
It gets much worse when I read, use the computer, or sit in dry, air-conditioned rooms, especially late in the day.
Yes, my mouth often feels quite dry as well, and I find myself needing water when I swallow dry foods.
I have some chronic stiffness in my fingers and knees from osteoarthritis, but I don't have severe morning back stiffness, mouth ulcers, or bowel trouble.
No, I have never had shingles, blisters on my forehead or nose, or herpes in my eyes.
No, I haven't had severe bouts of coughing, vomiting, or heavy lifting, and I don't take any blood thinners.
I think it might be dry eye syndrome or just part of getting older, perhaps related to my Sjogren's syndrome.
The constant scratchy and gritty feeling really bothers me throughout the evening, and I worry it might damage my eyes.
I would like to get a recommendation for soothing eye drops and find out what else I can do to keep my eyes comfortable.
I have never had glaucoma, cataracts, eye surgery, or similar eye issues before.
I was diagnosed with Sjogren's syndrome several years ago, and I also have osteoarthritis in my hands and knees.
I had my appendix removed when I was twenty-two, but I have had no other surgeries or hospital stays.
I take hydroxychloroquine 200 milligrams once a day for my Sjogren's, and occasionally acetaminophen for joint pain.
I don't have any allergies to medications or anything else.
I have never smoked in my life, and I only have an occasional glass of wine at celebrations.
I am retired and live with my husband, spending most of my days reading, doing crafts, and volunteering occasionally.
My mother had rheumatoid arthritis, but no one in my family has had glaucoma or other serious eye diseases.

exam.finding: Blood pressure is 124/78 mmHg, heart rate is 72 beats per minute, respiratory rate is 14 breaths per minute, body temperature is 36.6°C, and oxygen saturation is 99% on room air.
A well-appearing woman in no acute distress who blinks frequently.
Mild diffuse bilateral conjunctival injection without ciliary flush or subconjunctival hemorrhage; sclerae are white and non-icteric.

Visual acuity is 20/20 bilaterally; pupils are equal, round, and reactive; extraocular movements are intact and painless; no foreign body on eyelid eversion; fluorescein staining reveals bilateral punctate epithelial erosions with a reduced tear meniscus and no corneal ulcer.
Oral mucosa is mildly dry with decreased salivary pooling; no buccal ulcers or pharyngeal erythema.
Bilateral distal interphalangeal joints show mild bony enlargement without erythema, warmth, or active synovitis.
